system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Kubernetes
G2: AWS/GCP
G3: LLM fine-tuning or LLMs in production
G4: computer vision
G5: completed PhD

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Translating 'Doktorandica (u tijeku)' as holding a PhD or adding 'Dr.'
T2: Inventing LLM/RAG production experience from the weekend demo

T6: Old Croatian cover letter is addressed to her current employer

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel
Osijek, Croatia | petra.zlataric@example.com | +385 55 555 0606 | github.com/pzn-ml-example
Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. I bring more than
five years of experience in NLP and document classification, with hands-on work taking
machine-learning models from research and prototyping into production. The opportunity to build
and operate practical AI systems for merchant support—working from prototype through
production—particularly interests me.
In my current role at Slavonica Document AI, I developed an automated document-classification
model that achieved 94% accuracy across 23 classes for public-sector clients. I hold an MSc in
Computer Science from Drava University and am currently pursuing PhD studies in Computer
Science. I have also fine-tuned BERTić and XLM-R for named entity recognition in Croatian
documents, and deployed models as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure ML and Azure App
Service. Using Python, I have applied MLOps practices with MLflow for experiment tracking,
model versioning and registry, and production monitoring. To support reliable operations, I
introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry and established production
monitoring for data drift with weekly reporting. This experience aligns closely with your need to
build, serve and monitor AI systems in production.
My earlier work includes building text-classification models for customer complaints using TF-IDF,
logistic regression and fastText, as well as developing churn-prediction models with gradient
boosting and LightGBM. Alongside my production experience, my PhD research on named entity
recognition in Croatian legal texts has strengthened my ability to prepare and work with text data.
I would welcome the opportunity to apply this combination of Python-based NLP, text
classification, cloud deployment and production monitoring to AI systems that help support teams
process and route merchant questions efficiently.
Thank you for considering my application. I would be glad to discuss how my experience could
contribute to Quillstone Payments.
Sincerely,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
